clue.text: People in tents change ends and rush about

indicators.note: change ends tells us a letter moves from the back of the word to its front

parts.note: campers are people sleeping under canvas

explanation.surface: Campers dash around their tents in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change ends' takes the final S of CAMPERS and puts it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run about quickly and playfully, like a child or small animal.

clue.text: Head of state jumped when betrayed

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the word state

parts.note: hopped means jumped

explanation.surface: A president leapt up when stabbed in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOPPED is British slang for informed on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, a betrayal to the authorities.

clue.text: Foreign port worker with English (received pronunciation)

parts.note: a worker ant, the crossword's favourite worker
RP abbreviates Received Pronunciation, the standard British accent

explanation.surface: An overseas dock labourer who speaks posh English.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major Belgian seaport, foreign from the British setter's view.

clue.text: No press go abroad for forecasts

indicators.note: abroad suggests the letters of the words no press go are scattered

explanation.surface: Without journalists travelling overseas there are no predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Prognoses are predictions, especially of how an illness will develop.

clue.text: Retire, in case of rare delicacy

indicators.note: case of means the outside letters of the word rare, its shell

parts.note: a treat is a delicacy, something special to eat

explanation.surface: Withdraw from a rare tasty morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives RE, the first and last letters of 'rare'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw or fall back, as to retire does.

clue.text: Plunders newspaper captured by enemies

indicators.note: captured by means the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: foes are enemies
a rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: Raiders seize a newspaper office held by hostile forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Forages can mean raids or ravages in search of supplies, the old military sense of plundering.

clue.text: One very quietly escaped outside and went mad

indicators.note: outside means the escape word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: fled means escaped
I is the Roman numeral one
pp is pianissimo, the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone slipped out silently and then lost their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipped is slang for lost one's temper or reason, going crazy.

clue.text: Chap understood to be broadcasting

definitions.meaning: a man's first name, any fellow
the radio operator's word for 'message received'

explanation.surface: A man says he has got the message over the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is a man's name, and in radio procedure it means message received and understood.

clue.text: Tradesman who's good, but not so keen on working

parts.note: lazier means less inclined to work

explanation.surface: A workman who is decent but rather idle.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a craftsman who fits glass into windows.

clue.text: Set part of play on lines

parts.note: a scene is a division of a play
RY abbreviates railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Part of a play concerns lines learnt for the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is the stage set, not a verb or group.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenery is the painted backdrop and structures that form a stage set.

clue.text: Dismissed situation in military settlement

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out
a post is a job or position, a situation

explanation.surface: Someone sacked from a job ends up at a remote army base.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small detached camp or garrison far from the main force.

clue.text: One tearing off without a word of thanks?

definitions.text: One tearing off without a word of thanks?

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of the word tearing go astray and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rushes away without even saying thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TEARING rearranged give the answer, and the whole clue describes such a person: someone dashing away without thanking anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, one who never shows gratitude.

clue.text: Writer captured outward reserve of groom

indicators.note: captured means the pen holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: outward points to just the outside letters of the word reserve

explanation.surface: An author holds back on describing the bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outward' takes the first and last letters of 'reserve'. 'groom' looks like the bridegroom but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen is to tidy one's appearance or feathers carefully, a verb sense of grooming.

clue.text: Skill shown by former exercises tires terribly

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: terribly signals that the word tires is rearranged

explanation.surface: Experience shows that a former gym routine wears one out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges TIRES into RTISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is specialist know-how or mastery, a high level of skill.

clue.text: Down payment on lodge

definitions.meaning: a first instalment paid when buying something
as a verb, to place or leave something for safekeeping, as with a bank

explanation.surface: A first instalment paid on a holiday cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an initial sum paid up front, and to put money or valuables somewhere safe.

clue.text: Ruin of the French ancient city

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' before a plural
Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: A French ruin of a city from antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck it utterly, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Mark crosses Liverpool and Rotterdam in this vehicle

indicators.note: crosses means the mark spans the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
both are ports, examples of the plural word

explanation.surface: Mark drives between two great harbour cities in his fast motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a scar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports car is a fast low-slung automobile, a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Red china started working across borders

indicators.note: across means the first pair of pieces stretches over the borders, holding them inside
started picks out just the opening letter of the word china

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
rims are edges or borders

explanation.surface: Communist China began operating across its frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' gives C, the first letter of 'china', and C plus ON is laid 'across' RIMS. 'Red' looks political beside 'china' but is just the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of red.

clue.text: Politicians can bite following reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges ministers, so here the letters of can bite are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ministers can snap at each other after a government shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: A reshuffle is the British prime minister's rearranging of government ministers, which makes the anagram signal fit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet is the senior group of government ministers.

clue.text: Salary perhaps right for a recent arrival

parts.note: a salary is one example of income

explanation.surface: Pay might be fair for a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is a newcomer who has moved into an area.

clue.text: "Shades" is not found in "pests"

indicators.note: not found in means the word is is missing from the longer word

parts.note: nuisances are pests or annoyances

explanation.surface: Sunglasses are absent from a pest-control catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shades' looks like sunglasses; it means fine distinctions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuances are subtle differences or gradations in meaning or colour.

clue.text: Old people spend month in sort out

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
out signals the letters of the word sort are scrambled

parts.note: Jan is the short form of January

explanation.surface: Elderly folk take a month to sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters to TROS. 'Old people' suggests pensioners, but these are the citizens of ancient Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojans were the people of ancient Troy, an old nation of antiquity.

clue.text: Proceeds to say thanks to rulers

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
kings are rulers

explanation.surface: Moves on to express gratitude to the monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like a verb but is the noun: money taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money received by a business, its receipts.

clue.text: An early Christian porter drinking position

indicators.note: drinking means the beer takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a type of ale
a post is a position

explanation.surface: A doorman knocks back a drink at his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a doorman but is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is one of the twelve disciples sent out to preach in the first church.

clue.text: Wise move in a pest

indicators.note: move signals that the letters of in a pest are shifted around

explanation.surface: It is clever to act against a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means having great wisdom, a learned word for sage.

clue.text: Return to support course

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a track is a course, as for racing

explanation.surface: Going back to sponsor a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To backtrack is to retrace one's steps, going back the way one came.

clue.text: Mainly ups and downs found in features editor's returns

indicators.note: returns says the hidden letters are read backwards
found in says the letters sit inside the words features editor's

explanation.surface: Fluctuations appear in a magazine editor's reports.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'found' in the definition; it is the hidden-word indicator with 'in'. 'Mainly' means of the main (the sea), so the ups and downs are of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides are the regular rise and fall of the sea, the main in poetic usage.

clue.text: Soldiers left retreating across the capital of Ontario

indicators.note: across means the reversed piece stretches over the capital letter, holding it inside
retreating means the word for left is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the capital of means the first letter of the word Ontario

explanation.surface: Troops withdraw across Toronto, the capital of Ontario.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns PORT into TROP, and the O from 'capital of Ontario' sits inside it. The surface makes you think of Toronto.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, especially cavalry.

clue.text: Unsettled comedian lacked energy to be funny

indicators.note: to be funny signals the remaining letters are rearranged
lacked means a letter is taken away from the word comedian

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A stand-up who had no energy left struggled to raise laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacked' takes E out of COMEDIAN, leaving COMDIAN, which 'to be funny' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people wander without a fixed home, so they are not settled anywhere.

clue.text: Something to wear with impudence before match

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek or impudence
a tie is a match in a cup competition

explanation.surface: A cheeky fan's outfit for the big game.
explanation.walkthrough: NECK as impudence is British slang, as in 'what a neck!'; a TIE is a knockout football fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a strip of fabric worn knotted round a collar, a garment item.

clue.text: Has confidence outside hospital to get jabs

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to trust is to have confidence in someone
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient trusts the hospital to give vaccinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jabs' looks like vaccinations in this hospital scene, but means pokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrusts are sudden forceful pokes or stabs, just as jabs are.

clue.text: Draw back after waves become too much!

indicators.note: after places the first piece behind the second in the answer

parts.note: surf is breaking waves

indicators.note: back means the word for draw is read in reverse

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match

explanation.surface: Retreating after the breakers get too big for the swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes EIT. The surface suggests swimmers retreating from big waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess or overabundance, more than is needed.
